report.answer_text:
Liquid Glass is Apple's software design language. Apple developed it as a unified visual theme for the graphical interfaces across its operating systems.[1] It was unveiled at the WWDC 2025 keynote. At the same event, Apple also moved to year-based naming for all its operating systems.[2]
Core idea
It was the first time a single design language extended across iOS 26, iPadOS 26, macOS Tahoe 26, watchOS 26, and tvOS 26.[2] Apple's design talks also cover visionOS.
Alan Dye, Apple's VP of Human Interface Design, called it "our broadest software design update ever."[2]
Apple wanted to unify the look and feel of interface elements across devices with different window sizes and displays.[1]
How it looks and behaves
Apple describes the material as defined mainly by "lensing." The warping and bending of light through a transparent object signals its presence, motion, and form.[3]
Elements bend light, respond to input with depth and fluidity, and adapt to the content behind them.[4]
The material can change shape and size. For example, a text selection tooltip expands to show all its options in a vertical list.[1]
Controls and toolbars were redesigned to be concentric with the rounded corners of modern hardware.[2]
Influences
Apple said it drew on:[1]
macOS's Aqua design language[1]
the real-time Gaussian blurring in iOS 7[1]
the motion design of iPhone X[1]
the Dynamic Island[1]
the glass-like UI of visionOS[1]
Guidance for developers
It isn't meant for use everywhere. It works best for the navigation layer, and glass shouldn't be stacked on glass.[5]
There are two variants. Regular is the most versatile. Clear lacks the adaptive behaviors, so content below stays more visible.[5]
Legibility is a concern. Elements using Liquid Glass need clear separation from content.[6] Low-vision users may have trouble with contrast when refracted light replaces solid backgrounds.[5]
Reception
Some reviewers praised how it emulates the refraction and lensing of real glass, calling it visually sophisticated.[1] Accessibility and readability are the main concerns critics raise.
